This is different from asking whether a borough simply resembles its immediate neighbors -- instead, you are testing whether the COMBINED total (the borough together with its neighbors) is unusually large or small compared to the citywide average, regardless of how similar the borough is to any one neighbor individually.

Note: a borough whose own value is missing should not itself be reported as a hot or cold spot in your final answer. Note: dedicated spatial-statistics packages (pysal, esda, libpysal, geopandas, or similar) are NOT installed in this environment -- don't spend turns trying different import paths for them. Implement your chosen method directly using only pandas and numpy. If your method produces a z-score, use the standard critical values: |z| > 1.96 for 95% confidence, |z| > 2.576 for 99% confidence.

```python
DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/getisord/getisord_crime_second_half_2018.csv'
ADJACENCY_PATH = 'chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv'

# Load crime data

    borough = row['borough']

    if borough not in neighbor_dict:

    neighbor_dict[neighbor].add(borough)

# Check if all boroughs are in the neighbor_dict

for b in all_boroughs:
    if b not in neighbor_dict:
```

```python
# Calculate citywide mean and variance
city_mean = df_crime['crime_rate_value'].mean()
city_var = df_crime['crime_rate_value'].var(ddof=1)  # Sample variance
print("Citywide mean:", city_mean)
print("Citywide variance:", city_var)

# Prepare data for each borough
results = []
for _, row in df_crime.iterrows():
    borough = row['borough']
    crime_rate = row['crime_rate_value']
    neighbors = neighbor_dict.get(borough, set())
    
    # Check if all neighbors have non-missing crime rates
    valid_neighbors = True
    for n in neighbors:
        if df_crime[df_crime['borough'] == n]['crime_rate_value'].isnull().values.any():
            valid_neighbors = False
            break
    
    if not valid_neighbors:
        continue  # Skip if any neighbor has missing data
    
    # Sum local area (borough + neighbors)
    local_sum = crime_rate
    for n in neighbors:
        local_sum += df_crime[df_crime['borough'] == n]['crime_rate_value'].values[0]
    
    num_areas = 1 + len(neighbors)
    expected_sum = city_mean * num_areas
    variance_sum = city_var * num_areas
    z_score = (local_sum - expected_sum) / np.sqrt(variance_sum)
    
    results.append({
        'borough': borough,
        'local_sum': local_sum,
        'expected_sum': expected_sum,
        'z_score': z_score
    })

# Convert results to DataFrame
results_df = pd.DataFrame(results)
print("Results DataFrame:\n", results_df)
```
